nodes.label: AMA: Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.author: Mengjie Wu; Yihao Huang; et al. (Wuhan University; NUS; NTU)

nodes.label: Benign Context Construction
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Use fully benign safe proxy tasks that mirror the malicious prompt structure, because early sensitive keywords raise later refusal probability.

nodes.label: Controlled Semantic Shift
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Only in the final turn substitute benign elements with malicious ones while preserving learned structure, to keep semantic alignment with the malicious goal.

nodes.label: Structure-Semantics Decoupling
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Decompose harmful responses into structural format and malicious semantic core, distributing them across turns to exploit temporal flexibility.

nodes.label: Semantic Drift Problem
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: In prior multi-turn attacks the final response drifts from the original malicious intent even when harmful-looking, so is not a truly successful jailbreak.

nodes.label: Crescendo (Multi-Turn Escalation Attack)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Baseline multi-turn attack (Russinovich et al.) that starts general and incrementally steers dialogue toward harmful output by exploiting pattern-following.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Jailbreak (General Paradigm)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Progressively transitioning from benign queries to harmful objectives across turns is more effective than single-turn concealment of malicious intent.
